title: Subagent spawner + supporting modules

findings.title: parent_session_id_of JSON-parses a value that is always a key-string, so SubagentSpawned/SubagentReturned are never emitted
findings.summary: serde_json::from_str::<SessionKey> cannot parse the flat key-string ('agent:main:main') that the only production wiring site (run_loop/inner.rs:1054, to_key_string()) supplies, because SessionKey is an internally tagged enum. It returns None on every spawn, so both durable parent-log events are skipped and subagent_tool::recovery's event-log path is dead.
findings.failure_scenario: A background sub-agent completes, the daemon restarts, the model calls check_status(request_id). The in-memory tracker is empty and the parent log holds no SubagentReturned, so completed work with its output is reported as unknown and may be re-run.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the body with SessionKey::parse(raw) (the existing string reader, already used by gateway/orphan_notice.rs:37); add a to_key_string() round-trip guard and an assertion that a spawn writes SubagentSpawned into the parent log.

findings.title: IsolationMode::Worktree anchors on the server process cwd instead of the run's project root
findings.summary: repo_root comes from std::env::current_dir() on a long-lived daemon, while the main run path anchors on workspace_override/agent.workspace() and this same function reads crate::projects::current_project_root() at line 621. Either the spawn hard-fails with NotAGitRepo, or the child is isolated into and rebased against the wrong repository.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator delegates to an isolation:worktree agent while working in ~/code/svc-a; the daemon was launched from ~/code/tooling, so the child branches, edits, and builds ~/code/tooling and reports success.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer crate::projects::current_project_root() and fall back to current_dir(); add a guard asserting the worktree's repo_root() equals the run's project root when one is published.

findings.title: Inline MCP servers are spawned and advertised to the child but have no execution path
findings.summary: McpScope::provision starts real inline processes and their tools reach the child catalog through McpScopedToolService's list/dispatchable_list/describe/metadata_schema, but its execute arms forward only to the parent ('Stage I MVP: extras execution deferred to Task 12', mcp_scope_view.rs:67). The parent never knew the inline server (provision rejects name collisions with PluginRegistry), so every inline tool call resolves to tool-not-found. The routing the registrar's doc promises does not exist in the tree.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent def declares an inline MCP server; each spawn pays the process start and handshake, hands the child an uncallable catalog entry, and the child burns its iteration budget retrying before teardown.
findings.suggested_fix: Either route inline names (plugin_id == 'inline:<server>') to the owning InlineMcpHandle inside McpScopedToolService, or stop advertising them: filter inline_tools out of McpScope::tools() and fail provision loudly for Inline specs until execution lands.

findings.title: context_summary is silently discarded for every Fresh-mode agent, including explore/coder/researcher
findings.summary: build_effective_task prepends the summary only when context_mode == Summary. ContextMode defaults to Fresh and the three most-used shipped delegates declare none, while the subagent tool schema advertises context_summary unconditionally (loop_tool.rs:128). The model gets no error and no signal.
findings.failure_scenario: Parent passes a 2 KB context_summary to 'explore'; the child receives only the bare task, answers off-target, and the parent cannot attribute the miss to a dropped parameter.
findings.suggested_fix: Either honour an explicit caller summary regardless of context_mode, or make the veto observable (report the drop in the tool result, qualify the schema description, and set Summary on explore/coder/researcher).

findings.title: Worktree and MCP cleanup run only on the success path; errors fall to a blocking Drop
findings.summary: Both teardowns are gated on result.is_ok(), so timeout/cancel/error skip the async cleanup while still inside an async context. WorktreeHandle::drop then runs a synchronous git worktree remove --force on a tokio worker thread and emits leaked:true telemetry for an ordinary timeout; InlineMcpHandle::drop spawns an OS thread plus a fresh runtime per handle.
findings.failure_scenario: A worktree-isolated research child hits its 120s wall clock; the handle drops on a tokio worker, blocking it for the duration of a large-checkout git removal, and the trace stream reports a leak that did not occur.
findings.suggested_fix: Run scope.shutdown().await and h.cleanup().await unconditionally before returning, logging failures; keep Drop strictly as the panic/abort safety net.

findings.title: ensure_team check-then-create races into duplicate teams; the error fallback is inert without a UNIQUE constraint on teams.name
findings.summary: teams.name has no UNIQUE index (teams/store.rs:174), so concurrent ensure_team calls both insert and the create-error re-query never fires. get_team_by_name is a bare query_row with no ordering and no status filter, so lookups pick an arbitrary duplicate and a disbanded team is returned as live.
findings.failure_scenario: One turn fans out two parallel subagent send_message calls to team 'analysis'; two teams are created and the follow-up read_inbox resolves to the other row, reporting an empty inbox for delivered messages.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a unique index on teams(name) via a de-duplicating migration so the existing fallback becomes real, or use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(name) DO NOTHING plus a re-read in one transaction; decide explicitly whether get_team_by_name should exclude disbanded teams.

findings.title: spawn() is ~580 lines in a 1015-line file
findings.summary: spawn() spans lines 185-764 and owns admission, isolation provisioning, session seeding, prompt/provider/tool-service assembly, a 110-line HarnessDeps literal, run+timeout+panic isolation, event emission and two teardown paths — over the 500-line guideline in CODE_ORGANIZATION.md / P2.
findings.failure_scenario: No runtime failure; the length is what made the two exit-path defects above (B4-03, B4-05) hard to see during review and will do the same on the next change.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract provision_isolation(), build_child_deps() and teardown() helpers, following the existing build_context_triple precedent.

cross_cutting: Allowlist enforcement is sound: all six ToolService methods overridden, and act.rs:392 drives name repair from the already-filtered dispatchable_list, so case/separator/fuzzy repair cannot synthesize a denied name. tools/server/repair.rs's looser repairer has no callers outside its module.
All 21 SpawnerBase fields verified plumbed through AgentRuntime builders into execute_via_harness (runtime.rs:486-565); no dangling with_*.
thinking.rs is total and fail-closed; both production callers honour the reject contract. tool_sets.rs has no set math to get wrong and is pinned to canonical builtin names.
progress.rs verified; its 200-char preview truncates with chars().take(200), so no UTF-8 slice panic.
sub_agents/traits.rs round-trips (serde defaults missing Option fields to None) but carries no schema version field — fine intra-version, worth a written additive-only policy given the A2A boundary.

Per-agent MCP scope is additive, not restrictive: declaring mcp_servers does not confine the child to those servers; AllowlistToolService is the only narrowing layer. Documented, but the name invites the opposite reading.

SubagentReturned.summary can be empty by construction (final_text cleared for a pure-tool_use last message at mod.rs:814 + unwrap_or_default at :688), which recovery.rs:212 would render alongside a 'do NOT re-run' note. Latent until B4-01 is fixed; handle in the same change.

Cancellation coverage is good: the semaphore wait is biased-selected against the cancel token with a byte-exact error string matched by equality downstream. The only unguarded window is the subagent_semaphore:None path (tests / direct callers).
